inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed

facts.text: The project integrates multi-arm MuJoCo simulation designed as a plugin to mujoco_ros_pkg.
The README's tested configuration lists Ubuntu 22.04, ROS 2 Humble, Panda 4.2.2 and 4.2.1, libfranka 0.9.2 and MuJoCo 3.2.0.
The dual-arm simulator launch selects dual_scene.xml when the gripper is loaded and resolves it below franka_description/mujoco/franka.
The dual-arm simulator launch includes launch_mujoco_ros_server.launch and passes the selected scene to it as its modelfile argument.
The dual-arm documentation says dual_scene.xml is loaded for the dual-arm simulation.
The MuJoCo files are under mujoco/franka, and each robot body carries gravcomp=1 for gravity compensation.
For the multi-arm case the documentation defines all arms in a single XML file, like mj_dual.
Additional objects can be included in the scene by including a separate file such as objects.xml.
The scene model is named 'panda scene' and includes mj_dual.xml and objects.xml.
mj_dual sets the option timestep to 0.002 s.
The scene has two arm trees rooted at mj_left_link0 and mj_right_link0, at y +0.26 and -0.26.
The right arm has the same seven hinge-joint ranges as the left arm.
The finger default class declares a slide joint with range 0 to 0.04 m.
Each hand carries two joints of class finger: mj_left_finger_joint1/2 and mj_right_finger_joint1/2.
The finger joints are coupled by fixed tendons with coefficient 0.5 and by joint equality constraints.

mj_dual.xml's actuator block has, per arm, seven torque motors with ctrllimited true (ctrlrange -87 87 for joints 1 to 4 and -12 12 for joints 5 to 7), seven position servos (kp 10) and seven velocity servos (kv 1) that declare no ctrlrange, and a general gripper channel of class panda with ctrlrange 0 255: 44 channels in all.
objects.xml adds a free-joint box (obj_box_01) and a mocap sphere (sphere_01).
The simulation interface handles n >= 1 Panda robots and exposes the same ROS 2 interfaces as the real robot.

The documentation says the real-robot interface FrankaMultiHardwareInterface wraps libfranka to connect to the robot, its control callbacks implement no logic of their own, and all safety features and command calculation must be handled by the controller.
.gitmodules declares mujoco_ros_pkgs as a git submodule from github.com/tenfoldpaper/mujoco_ros_pkgs, branch wip_ros_control_humble.
The MuJoCo hardware plugin initialises every arm's torque, position and velocity actuators to off: torque flag 0 and servo gains 0.

When a mode switch is pending, perform_command_mode_switch turns on only the actuator set of the arm's control mode (torque flag 1, position-servo kp 100 or velocity-servo kv 10) and zeroes the other two sets; mode None zeroes all three.

write returns an error for a non-finite effort, position or velocity command and writes data.ctrl only for the actuator set of the arm's control mode, plus the gripper channel when the arm has a gripper.
The multi-mode controller's Panda limits give the maximum joint velocity as 2.1750 rad/s for joints 1 to 4 and 2.6100 rad/s for joints 5 to 7.

gaps: the fake is a package-local stand-in for the mujoco Python module, not MuJoCo: it parses the MJCF and its includes for the actuator control ranges, joint dimensions and option timestep, but its step is a placeholder first-order motion, not the model's dynamics

the dual scene has 44 actuator channels in document order (per arm seven torque motors, seven position servos, seven velocity servos and one gripper); the fake reports all 44, the 28 servos as not ctrl-limited as MuJoCo compiles them, and its placeholder motion applies every channel at once, as the bare MJCF does without the upstream plugin's gain switching

the fake resolves no mesh, inertia, contact, friction, tendon, equality or gravity compensation; the free-joint box, the mocap sphere and the two-arm contact geometry are counted in qpos/qvel but are not simulated

the fake resets qpos to the model's qpos0 (zero arm and finger joints, the free box at its body pose) and qvel and ctrl to zero, while the upstream simulation sets the arm joints from ros2_control initial_position parameters; the fake does not read those parameters, and zero lies outside the ranges of joints 4 and 6

MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine; the driver's sim backend would import mujoco and load the same file, but it was not run
the fake has no mj_getState, mj_setState or mj_stateSize, so snapshots use the bridge's basic profile (time, qpos, qvel, ctrl and act), not the full MuJoCo integration state
no viewer, rendering, camera, contact sensor or actuator force is exposed; only the cap.world.step and cap.world.reset integration state and control vector are served

the upstream ros2_control controller manager, gripper action servers and rosbridge layer are not part of this world driver; the raw actuator vector is exposed instead of the upstream's joint/controller interface
the free box and the mocap sphere are not externally placed; the fake has no reset scenario or seed control beyond the bridge's configured seed
no physical robot is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware

safe_state.description: No step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the last integration state is kept and remains readable, and the lockstep simulation does not advance between steps. The latch is software and the simulation has no physical stop.
